readout_other: Tail EMG: motor-response success rate, latency, duration, and normalized amplitude
direction_notes: LIPUS reliably evoked tail muscle EMG (motor) responses; response success rate and EMG amplitude decreased and latency/duration increased stepwise as the isoflurane concentration/body-weight ratio increased, with no responses at the highest dose tested (0.024%/g).
safety_notes: Bioheat modelling using the study's maximum ultrasonic intensity (2 W/cm2) and pulse duration (0.2 s) estimated a maximum temperature rise of ~3.67x10^-3 degrees C, judged far below the threshold for thermal bioeffects.

exposures.label: LIPUS to mouse motor cortex across 11 isoflurane doses

timing.protocol_description: The PRF, SD (stimulation duration) and TBD (tone-burst duration) of the ultrasound were 1 kHz, 200 ms and 0.3 ms, respectively. Mice were anesthetized with one isoflurane concentration for 10 min before LIPUS, then LIPUS was performed for 5 min while tail EMG was recorded, followed by 5 more minutes of anesthesia; each mouse was then tested with the next of 11 isoflurane doses (0.1% to 0.6% in 0.05% steps, corresponding to ratios of 0.004%/g to 0.024%/g of body weight).

source_quotes.n_subjects: We used eleven BALB/c mice for the experiments (all male, body weights \~ 25 g, Beijing Vital River Laboratory Animal Technology Co., Ltd. China).

flags.reason: Paper labels this value 'SD' (stimulation duration) rather than a named sonication/train duration; a later thermal-safety calculation independently uses 'pulse duration t=0.2 s', consistent with this value being the length of one uninterrupted train.
Not stated by the paper; arithmetic from TBD (0.3 ms) and PRF (1 kHz) would imply ~30%, but this was not computed here per instructions.
Paper does not state whether the reported Isppa (~2 W/cm2) is a free-field or in-situ value; placed in unspecified_domain.

Each of the 11 mice appears to have been tested at all 11 isoflurane doses (matching N=11 at every ratio), but the paper does not explicitly state the number of sessions per subject or whether doses were tested on separate days.
